change_reason: V2 confirmed that a larger output cap alone does not prevent Kimi round-one verbosity. V3 stages the prompt so round one receives only a tiny provisional response contract and round two receives the detailed evidence schema.
hypothesis: For this bounded exact task, heterogeneous Joint Cognition may improve criterion completion or correct an error relative to the strongest selected single participant.
interpretation_rule: One experiment can show a correction or failure mode but cannot establish general superiority.

task.active_focus: A coin gives H with probability 2/3 and T with probability 1/3. Starting before any tosses, find the expected waiting time for the first consecutive HTH. Use states equal to the longest current suffix that is a prefix of HTH; report the transitions, first-step equations, exact fraction, and decimal value.
task.round_protocol: Round 1 is provisional. Do not resolve the focus until a later checkpoint exposes prior semantic evidence. In round 2, inspect prior claims, raise a precise objection when warranted, correct errors, and submit criterion evidence only for claims you can verify.

criteria.description: State the exact expected waiting time and its decimal equivalent.
Give all H/T transitions for empty, H, and HT, including the H-to-H self-overlap.
Give one correct first-step expectation equation for each nonterminal state.
Substitute the solved values into every equation and verify the exact result independently.

conditions.selection_rule: Kimi K2.6 was preregistered before outputs as the strongest validated participant available within the bounded structured-response protocol.

stop_conditions: Stop before network access unless all three saved participant profiles and prices match this manifest.
Stop after two rounds per condition; make no retries, rebases, substitutions, or extra synthesis calls.
Stop and report partial evidence if any provider fails.
